title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Singapore: Fast Route Search ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra meet in the middle to find the shortest path faster than a single-source search. This visualization shows how real route planning engines scale by cutting the explored area dramatically.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional Dijkstra: How Modern Route Planners Scale — meet-in-the-middle route speedup ⚡ Can you “halfish” the shortest path? 

Here’s the idea: instead of running Dijkstra from just the start, we run it from BOTH start and goal. Each frontier expands via a priority queue, and we stop when the best possible combined distance is locked in—so the explored graph shrinks massively.

🔧 In the video, notice how: 
• Forward search grows outward from the origin
• Backward search grows outward from the destination
• The paths converge at an optimal meeting node (or edge)

✅ Takeaway for software engineering: fewer nodes popped from the heap = faster shortest path at scale, especially on large road networks.

Debate question: In practice, when would you choose bidirectional Dijkstra over A* (or vice versa) for real route planning engines?
